svg.text: Destination, the same batch. code_seed and batch_id rebuild the three rows of G.

g.text: rebuilt locally: row of p1 is (g0 g1 g2 g3 g4 g5 g6 g7), and likewise one row each for p4 and p6
a packet that arrived: batch 12, coefficient (c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7), payload z

svg.text: That packet gives one equation for each chosen source packet. For p1 the coefficient is the dot product

g.text: g0 c0 + g1 c1 + g2 c2 + g3 c3 + g4 c4 + g5 c5 + g6 c6 + g7 c7

svg.text: The right-hand side is z. The same dot product with the row of p4, and with the row of p6, gives their equations.
At the source, before any relay, the coefficient was a column of the identity, so this dot product was a single entry of G.
A solved batch substitutes those source packets into every other batch that contains them. Inactivation finishes whatever peeling leaves.
